newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money falls to 4.0/5.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money falls to 4.0/5.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money fell to 4.0/5.0 percent from 7.0/9.0 percent on Tuesday morning on ample liquidiy, dealers said.
They said liquidity was in excess despite a neutral central bank money policy. One local bank dealer said it could be due to carry-forward liquidity which kept the market flush.
Longer-term rates softened too, with one-week money edging down to 10.5 percent, two to 11.5 percent, one-month to 12.75 and three to 13.5 percent.
The central bank offered one-week bilateral papers (SBIs) at 6.5, two-week at 8.5 percent, one-month at 10.25 percent and three-month at 11.25 percent.
Dealers said swap rates were also edging down following ample short-term funds. Overnight swaps fell to par level.
The average overnight interbank rates on Monday was 9.16 percent, compared with 10.82 percent last Friday.
Bond dealers said the market seemed to have quietened down for now ahead of the general elections on Thursday.
"We haven't had any deal yet in the past two days. The market is pretty quiet," one bond dealer said.
